tldr: CIBC is set to offer Canadian retail investors access to the Anthropic IPO through a CDR, while B3 in Brazil already lists a sub-R$100 BDR. Wealthsimple is also opening a CAD stablecoin beta with 3.25% promotional rewards, and Canadian banks continue to pay big cash bonuses for new chequing customers.
themes: Retail access to hot US IPOs via local depositary receipts
Fractional, low-minimum investing for retail users
Fintechs gaining bank status and expanding products

highlights.headline: CIBC will launch an Anthropic Canadian Depositary Receipt following the US IPO, and its CDR lineup now stands at 145. B3 in Brazil is launching an Anthropic BDR at the same time as the Nasdaq debut, with a minimum investment under R$100.
highlights.why: A direct competitor is turning access to a marquee US IPO into a Canadian-dollar, low-ticket product. Simplii customers will expect similar access, so the team should check what CDR and IPO access its trading platform offers.

highlights.headline: Wealthsimple opened a beta for CADD with 3.25% promotional rewards.
highlights.why: Wealthsimple is a direct competitor pairing a new CAD-denominated digital product with a rewards rate. This sets a new benchmark for yield and product novelty among digitally minded Canadians.

highlights.headline: BMO is offering up to $1,100 in cash plus Walmart+ for up to 12 months on Performance Chequing. Scotiabank is offering up to $1,000 for moving pay, and $175 for students.
highlights.why: Big-bank chequing acquisition offers are escalating, with bonuses tied to payroll switching. This is a direct benchmark for Simplii's own welcome and payroll-switch incentives.

highlights.headline: Nubank received Brazilian Central Bank approval for a banking charter through the Banco Porto Real acquisition, keeping its brand. It also reportedly reached all 50 US states in the first weeks of Nubank U.S.
highlights.why: A digital-first challenger is gaining full bank status and expanding into the US market. This reinforces the category shift toward fintechs holding charters, and Nubank's entry into North America is worth watching.
